findings.title: Classic‑ASP member deletion without role check

evidence.why: auth guard only checks session, no role

evidence.code: conn.Execute "DELETE FROM members WHERE member_id = " & Request.QueryString("member_id")
evidence.why: privileged action, no role check

findings.attack_scenario: A logged‑in user can delete any member by supplying a member_id in the query string.
findings.impact: Any authenticated user can delete arbitrary members, including administrators.
findings.recommendation: Add a server‑side role check that ensures the current user has the 'Admin' role before executing the delete.
findings.fix_example: If Not CheckRole("Admin") Then Response.Status = "403 Forbidden" : Response.End

verification.notes: The included `auth.asp` only verifies that a session exists; it does not enforce a role. The delete statement uses the `member_id` from the query string without any role validation. Any authenticated user can delete any member, including administrators. The BFLA is confirmed.

consensus.rationale: No role check found in authentication guard.

findings.title: Spring MVC delete user action missing admin role check

evidence.why: no @PreAuthorize on method

findings.attack_scenario: Any authenticated user can delete any user account.
findings.impact: Privilege escalation to delete arbitrary user accounts.
findings.recommendation: Add @PreAuthorize("hasRole('ADMIN')") to the delete method.
findings.fix_example: @PreAuthorize("hasRole('ADMIN')") @RequestMapping(value = "/{id}/delete", method = RequestMethod.POST) public String delete(@PathVariable("id") Long id) { … }

verification.notes: Spring Security configuration restricts all `/admin/**` URLs to users with the `ADMIN` role via `antMatchers("/admin/**").hasRole("ADMIN")`. The DeleteUser action is therefore protected by this global rule, mitigating the reported BFLA.

consensus.rationale: Global security rule provides the missing role check.
